chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever resides in the City (Madinah) for a month while intending to perform Hajj, and then it occurs to him to depart via a route other than the one the people of the City take, then his Ihram (state of consecration) must be from a distance of six miles."
And for one who assumes Ihram via the route of the City, it is not permissible to switch the Ihram from al-Shajara to Dhat Irq.

key_terms.إِحْرَامُهُ: His state of Ihram (consecration for Hajj)
key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: Al-Shajara (a specific Miqat station near Medina)
key_terms.طَرِيقِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ: The route of the people of Medina (standard Miqat route)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct Miqat for a resident of Medina who wants to perform Hajj via a non-standard route?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Miqat for Medina residents, specifically addressing the scenario where one stays for a month and departs via a non-standard route, requiring Ihram at six miles from the city. It further establishes that travelers on the standard route cannot shift their Ihram station from Al-Shajara to Dhat Irq, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the fixed nature of these boundaries for locals. This ruling underscores the precision required in Hajj rituals to ensure the validity of consecration according to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.
